Let me measure peak memory. `/usr/bin/time` isn't available; let me use a Python wrapper with resource.getrusage(RUSAGE_CHILDREN).

Let me also run the fuzzer with the live trie enabled to check stability across many random cases.

arguments.command:
cd /workspace && python3 - <<'PY'
import json,subprocess,sys,resource,os,time
sys.path.insert(0,'/workspace/tmp/tests')
src=open('/workspace/tmp/tests/maxtest.py').read().replace("\nif __name__ == '__main__':","\nif False:")
g={'__name__':'bt','__file__':'/workspace/tmp/tests/maxtest.py'}
exec(compile(src,'maxtest','exec'),g)
req=g['build'](3)
body=json.dumps(req,separators=(',',':'))
t0=time.time()
p=subprocess.run([sys.executable,'run.py'],input=body.encode(),cwd='/workspace',capture_output=True,timeout=600)
ru=resource.getrusage(resource.RUSAGE_CHILDREN)
print('elapsed %.2f  maxrss %.1f MB' % (time.time()-t0, ru.ru_maxrss/1024.0))
PY
for s in 5 6 7; do timeout 900 python3 tmp/tests/fuzz.py $s 10 2>&1 | grep -E "^(FAIL|fuzz)"; done
